data.narrative:
Tempo is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Nima Rahmatian, Kelvin Randhir, Joerg Petrasch, and Alessandro Bo, having raised $50M to date. The comparable universe in Climate & Energy spans 9 private peers (including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen) and 1 public reference point (LNZA), though narrow peer filtering by stage and valuation tier yielded insufficient data for median multiples analysis.

Valuation analysis relies on stage-progression methodology, which applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement to the $50M capital raised as a proxy baseline. This approach yields an implied value of $100M. Peer-median analysis was not applicable given only 9 same-sector peers exist without sufficient density at identical or adjacent stages and comparable valuation tiers to support robust multiples triangulation.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $85M to $115M, with a median point of $100M. Key uncertainties include the lack of narrow peer comparables at similar stage and valuation density, which limits confidence in derived multiples and makes stage-progression multiplier selection the primary driver of the range. Any adjustment would require additional market data on recent Climate & Energy Series A outcomes or more granular peer progress metrics.
